children: EUROPE BEFORE THE BELL: STOXX SET FOR 2% WEEKLY FALL
The STOXX 600 is set for a 2% weekly drop, its biggest since mid April — a 12% weekly jump in front-month European natural gas prices (TFMBMc1) a near-10% jump in Brent
and 17 basis points on the 10-year Bund yield in the week so far will do that for you. (DE10YT=RR)
Futures are pointing to slight gains on Friday, with energy prices actually slightly lower on the day, though how long that respite will last remains to be seen.
The short-term picture will all come down to U.S. inflation data due 1230 GMT, a hot print would come close to cementing bets on a Federal Reserve rate hike, and send short dated bond yields higher.
A softer print might offer some relief to the bond market.
CPI likely increased 0.4% last month after edging up 0.1% in July, a Reuters survey of economists predicted. Core CPI is expected to have increased 0.2%.

The medium term picture is all about energy, and the Middle East, however. The latest worry for markets is news Iran-aligned Houthis have gained further leverage over the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, the southern outlet of the Red Sea and one of the world's most important shipping routes.
In terms of company news, Berlin will push for Commerzbank
to retain its German identity with a domestic stock market listing and to protect jobs, two people familiar with the matter said,
